method: Random generated items re-solved by hand (Python, NumPy and SQL outputs traced and checked against the computed answer; statistics recomputed; facts against NCERT Informatics Practices class 11): 3 per chapter file incl. mocks (seed 17, 27 items; seed 404, 27 items) and 2 per chapter file (seed 2026, 18 items), plus one hand-checked variant of each new computed family (stat_written, sd_written, sd_mcq, median_even, np_std, np_genfromtxt, insert_write, dml_case, ip_loop_case, null_q); every code, NumPy and SQL output in the bank is produced at build time by running it (SQL on sqlite3 with class 11 queries only: no aggregates or division, so the result matches MySQL), every family is smoke-tested over 60 seeds, and the whole bank was scanned for out-of-syllabus code (dictionary pop(), string methods, break/continue, def, tuples)
fixes: source-extract item asked to explain in part (ii) the term that answers part (i) ('domain'); such variants are now regenerated (guard in g11_computer_science_kit.no_open_pick, used by CS and IP)
a program-writing answer for a program with no input read 'Sample run: input  → output'; it now reads '# Output: ...'
whole-bank scan: 4 source-extract items had an open part (i) worded 'Which of the following ...' with no options shown; these variants are now regenerated
DML case increased marks by 100 (unrealistic); the increment now suits the column (Marks + 5, Salary + 1000, Price + 10)
SQL output MCQs had too few distinct distractors; added the query without its WHERE clause, the reversed ORDER BY and row-dropped results as distractors
NumPy MCQ distractors no longer use token-reversed text; they keep the printed array layout with changed numbers
